GET_SESSION_NAME.dispatch: IPCObjectStub::SendRequest switches GET_SESSION_NAME to DBinderGetSessionName before ordinary OnRemoteRequest dispatch (ipc_object_stub.cpp approximately lines 439-475).
GET_SESSION_NAME.handler_guard: DBinderGetSessionName only requires IPCSkeleton::IsLocalCalling(); it does not require IsSamgrCall or compare caller UID/PID with an authorized identity. Binder local-transport predicate is not an app authorization check.
GET_SESSION_NAME.data_flow: Handler calls this stub's GetSessionName(). That obtains the process SAMGR proxy and calls IPCObjectProxy::GetGrantedSessionName(). SAMGR-side GetGrantedSessionName uses IPCSkeleton::GetCallingPid()/GetCallingUid() for the requesting service process, constructs DBINDER_SOCKET_NAME_PREFIX + uid + '_' + pid via CreateSessionName, and returns it. Thus a caller of the public helper receives a session-name string derived from the target service process UID/PID, rather than the original Binder caller identity or an arbitrary parcel-supplied identity.
GET_SESSION_NAME.proxy_route: IPCObjectProxy::GetSessionName() directly invokes SendRequestInner(false, GET_SESSION_NAME, ...) and reads the reply string; ordinary public SendRequest's transaction-code guard is bypassed by this typed helper.
GET_SESSION_NAME.api_export: GetSessionName is declared public in ipc_object_proxy.h and explicitly listed in libipc_single_map global exports. ipc_single BUILD.gn selects this map as version_script; ipc_core is installed in platformsdk. The standard SDK/ABI route therefore does not exclude ordinary app-linked native callers.
GET_SESSION_NAME.sensitivity: The returned DBinder session name incorporates the target service process UID and PID. This can expose service-process identity metadata to an ordinary app that already holds an IPCObjectProxy to that stub. No evidence in this bounded source review establishes that the metadata is security-sensitive in the target product, exploitable impact beyond information disclosure, or whether another supported API already reveals the same values.

candidate.claim: A standard-exported IPCObjectProxy::GetSessionName sends a local special transaction accepted without caller identity authorization; the reply is a DBinder name embedding the target service process UID/PID. Ordinary native apps holding a proxy can therefore retrieve those process identifiers.
candidate.promotion_gate: Second layer must decide whether target service UID/PID is protected information and materially unavailable to ordinary app callers, and whether the call is intended to be callable by any holder of a proxy. Do not report as confirmed vulnerability absent that impact assessment.

GET_PID_UID.handler_guard: Requires IsLocalCalling() and IsSamgrCall(); latter indicates receiver process registry/SAMGR state, not authenticated caller identity.
GET_PID_UID.response: Writes the receiving process getpid() and getuid() to reply.
GET_PID_UID.public_reachability: No typed IPCObjectProxy helper for GET_PID_UID was found in the pinned header/source; the public generic SendRequest rejects special transaction values above MAX_TRANSACTION_ID (except DUMP_TRANSACTION). GET_PID_UID is not in the ipc_single export map. No standard ordinary-app route to this handler was found in reviewed source.

independent_review_requests_for_T38: Verify nested Binder caller identity at SAMGR: the pid/uid used by GetGrantedSessionName must be the target service process identity, not the original app identity.
Verify ordinary app possession of an IPCObjectProxy to a typical system service and whether GetSessionName is part of the published platformsdk/native API contract.
Assess whether the returned DBinder session name (UID_PID) is materially sensitive and whether the same service PID/UID is available through supported APIs, logs, or service discovery.

For GET_PID_UID, independently confirm the absence of a public helper/export and that generic SendRequest code-range validation blocks direct invocation before transport; distinguish IsSamgrCall receiver-state from caller authorization.
Do not infer deployed-product impact from source/SDK metadata alone; state any remaining product-build pairing gap.
overall_verdict: One low-severity, conditional metadata-disclosure candidate for GET_SESSION_NAME is retained for second-layer review because the standard native helper is exported and returns target service UID/PID encoded as a session name. GET_PID_UID has no ordinary-app route found. No tests, PoC, or product code changes were made.
